name: 4.5 Flat-Plane V8
notes: Variant: Ferrari 458 Italia coupe (project F142, 2009-2015, US model years 2010-2015; F136 FB engine; owner's manual rating 416 kW / 565 HP at 9,000 rpm, European rating 419 kW / 570 CV including 5 CV of ram effect) with the 7-speed F1 dual-clutch gearbox (rear transaxle, no torque converter) on the standard rear 295/35 ZR20 tyre (rear-wheel drive with E-Diff 3; the optional 285/35 ZR20 winter tyre is not modelled). Gearbox data are from Ferrari's 458 Italia Owner's Manual (2nd Edition January 2010, p. 27): gear ratios 3.077/2.185/1.626/1.286/1.028/0.839/0.693 and one differential/bevel gear pair ratio of 5.143 shared by every gear, so overall ratio = gear x 5.143 (no other fixed gear stage is listed). The 458 Spider owner's manual (p. 27) lists the same gear ratios, bevel gear pair ratio, F 136 FB engine and 9,200 rpm limit. Displacement conflict: the 2009 brochure and the January 2010 owner's manual print 4,499 cm3 (274.5 cu in), while ferrari.com, the later 458 Spider and 458 Speciale owner's manuals and the EPA engine code 'F136FB/4497' give 4,497 cc, which is also what 94 x 81 mm x 8 cylinders gives (4,496.7 cc); 4.497 L is used. Combustion: Ferrari describes a 90-degree V8 with a flat-plane crankshaft (180 degrees between the throws) whose 'even firing order between banks' suits the exhaust manifolds, so each bank fires every 180 deg and the two banks alternate at even 720/8 = 90 deg intervals (first principles). Entries are listed in firing order; bank 0 = the bank whose cylinder fires first (bank 0 at 0/180/360/540, bank 1 at 90/270/450/630). No readable Ferrari document gives the cylinder-numbered firing order: forum posts reportedly quoting the Ferrari service manual give 1-8-3-6-4-5-2-7 in Ferrari's numbering (cylinders 1-4 right bank front to rear, 5-8 left bank rear to front), which is 1-5-3-7-4-8-2-6 if both banks are numbered front to rear; either way the banks strictly alternate, so the angle/bank data do not depend on it (bank 0 would be the right bank, cylinders 1-4). RPM: redline 9,000 rpm = Ferrari's 'maximum revs per minute' (brochure; peak power is also at 9,000 rpm); limiter rpm 9,200 = the owner's manual 'Maximum RPM 9200 RPM (with limiting device)'; the optional steering-wheel shift LEDs light at 5,500/6,250/7,000/7,750/8,920 rpm. Estimated (not published in the sources used): idle 900 rpm; limiter type fuel-soft with 150 rpm hysteresis; shift time 0.10 s (DCT default: Ferrari quotes a zero 'gear shifting time' defined as the overlap of the two clutches' opening and closing phases, i.e. no torque interruption, but no shift duration). EPA Test Car Lists MY2010-2015 carry a single 458 row (test vehicle ZFF67NHB000171765, labelled '458 Italia Spyder' in every year including MY2010; engine code F136FB, 7 gears, rear drive, axle 5.14, N/V 43.5): it equals 7th x 5.143 on 295/35ZR20 within 1 % (model 43.91 rpm/mph) and is used in the EPA N/V check. In the same model 7th gear at 9,000 rpm gives about 205 mph (330 km/h), consistent with Ferrari's statement that seventh gear takes the car up to its >325 km/h maximum speed.

90-degree V8 with a flat-plane (180-degree) crankshaft: each bank fires like an inline four every 180 deg and the banks are offset by the 90 deg vee angle, so firings are evenly 720/8 = 90 deg apart with the banks strictly alternating (first principles)
